title: The pair of valuation extensions factors through $X_{12}$
statement:
Let $A$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$. Suppose
$\operatorname{Spec}(K)\to U_1\cap U_2$ is an $S$-morphism and let
$g_i\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_i$ be extensions. Then the pair

$$
(g_1,g_2)\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_1\times_SX_2
$$

factors through $X_{12}$.

proof.text:
The two generic maps have the same image in $U$, so their pair lands in
$V_1\times_UV_2=V_{12}$. Composing with the canonical image-factor map
gives a factorization of the generic pair through $X_{12}$. The map
$A\to K$ is injective because a valuation ring is a domain. Apply
[lemma-nagata-valuation-factor-closed] to the closed immersion
$X_{12}\hookrightarrow X_1\times_SX_2$ and the morphism
$(g_1,g_2)\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_1\times_SX_2$. It extends the
generic factorization to all of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $A$ be a domain with fraction field $K$. Let
$\eta\colon\operatorname{Spec}(K)\to U_1\cap U_2$ be a morphism and let
$g_i\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_i$ be morphisms whose restrictions
to $\operatorname{Spec}(K)$ equal $\eta$ followed by the embedding
$U_i\hookrightarrow X_i$, and such that $g_1$ and $g_2$ induce the same
morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to S$. Then the pair

$$
(g_1,g_2)\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_1\times_SX_2
$$

factors through $X_{12}$: there is a morphism
$l\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_{12}$ with $p_1\circ l=g_1$ and
$p_2\circ l=g_2$.

proof.text:
Since $g_1$ and $g_2$ agree over $S$, they define
$(g_1,g_2)\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_1\times_SX_2$. Both generic
maps come from $\eta$ through $U_i\subseteq V_i$, and $\psi_i$ restricts to
the inclusion on $U_i$, so their compositions with $\psi_1$ and $\psi_2$
agree in $U$; hence the generic pair lands in $V_1\times_UV_2=V_{12}$.
Composing with the canonical image-factor map gives a factorization of the
generic pair through $X_{12}$. Apply
[lemma-nagata-valuation-factor-closed] to the domain $A$, the closed
immersion $X_{12}\hookrightarrow X_1\times_SX_2$ and the morphism
$(g_1,g_2)$. It extends the generic factorization to a morphism
$l\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X_{12}$, and $p_i\circ l=g_i$ because
$p_i$ is the restriction of the $i$-th projection.
